record.original_question: Let β(n)+iγ(n) denote the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. If for every positive z != 1 the sequence ((log z)/(2π))γ(n), n >= 0, is uniformly distributed modulo 1, do the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function form a random sequence?

evidence.quote: The non-trivial zeros of Riemann's Zeta function are uniformly distributed ... then for every positive z != 1, the sequence ... is uniformly distributed modulo 1. Do non-trivial zeros of Riemann's Zeta function form a random sequence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho_n = \beta(n) + i\gamma(n)$, $n \geq 0$, denote the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$, listed with $\gamma(n) > 0$ in non-decreasing order. Suppose that for every real number $z > 0$ with $z \neq 1$, the sequence
$$\left( \frac{\log z}{2\pi}\, \gamma(n) \right)_{n \geq 0}$$
is uniformly distributed modulo $1$ (i.e., for every interval $[a,b] \subseteq [0,1)$,
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \#\left\{ 0 \leq n < N : \left\{ \tfrac{\log z}{2\pi} \gamma(n) \right\} \in [a,b] \right\} = b - a,$$
where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$).

Under this hypothesis, does the sequence of non-trivial zeros $(\rho_n)_{n \geq 0}$ of $\zeta(s)$ form a random sequence (in the sense of algorithmic randomness, e.g. Martin-Löf randomness of a suitable binary encoding of the sequence)?
artifact.category_tag: Riemann zeta zeros and algorithmic randomness
artifact.status_search_result: The hypothesis that the normalized non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ are uniformly distributed modulo 1 (a conjecture of Odlyzko, equivalent to the stated condition for all $z>0$, $z\neq 1$) remains unproved, even under the Riemann Hypothesis; only partial results (e.g. for restricted ranges of the parameter, via Piatetski-Shapiro type theorems) are known. The further question of whether such uniform distribution implies algorithmic randomness of the zeros does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the distribution (mod 1) of the normalized zeros of the Riemann Zeta-function
status_evidence.snippet: Odlyzko conjectured that the normalized zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are uniformly distributed mod 1; this is far from being proved, even assuming RH. Partial results are obtained for restricted ranges.
status_evidence.claim: The uniform distribution mod 1 hypothesis on normalized zeta zeros is still open.

status_evidence.title: The Uniform Distribution Modulo One of Certain Subsequences of Ordinates of Zeros of the Zeta Function
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper studying uniform distribution mod 1 of subsequences of ordinates of zeros, indicating the general problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2023) work continues to address only partial cases, confirming the general problem is open.
